Name: Ubotica Technologies
Description:
Founded in 2016, Ubotica Technologies is the leader in SPACE AI, providing the intelligence that makes satellites truly smart. Our onboard processing solutions enable satellites to think, see, and act autonomously, delivering real-time, actionable insights while reducing data bottlenecks and latency.

We collaborate with leading space organizations, including NASA, and ESA to advance the capabilities of autonomous satellite operations. From intelligent space cameras to autonomous satellite collaboration, we are shaping the future of space intelligence.

Discover how Ubotica is revolutionizing satellite operations—visit our website to explore our cutting-edge SPACE AI solutions.

Name: ICAD - International Centre for Astronautical Development
Description:
The International Centre for Astronautical Development (ICAD) is a non-income-generating, not-for-profit organization that functions through an international volunteer community with a shared vision.

Our mission is to ignite global space sector interest and capability, specifically directing our efforts towards under-represented regions of the world. We are working on various approaches to achieve this goal, including an outreach program, project-based joint ventures within the field of space medicine, and a mentorship program. This threefold approach allows us to create change across all generations for the most sustainable results, all bringing us one step closer to becoming an interplanetary species. 

MENTORSHIP
Our mentorship program reaches postgraduates and established professionals, regardless of age or industry experience. This will guide the development of local space start-ups in regions with emerging or non-existent space sectors, to increase their chances of maturation.

OUTREACH
ICAD’s outreach program aims to inspire and educate the younger generation, from toddlers to young adults, to pursue careers in the space industry for generational continuity. Our vision is to grow this outreach program throughout all under-represented countries in the Space industry.

SPACE MEDICINE
Our Space Medicine division (IRSHAD - Institute of Research into Space Health and Astronautical Development) works on a project-by-project basis. Our goal is to make commercial space flight more accessible internationally; to bring scientific knowledge to the general public; and to build space medicine knowledge in under-represented communities.

If you would like to join our team or learn more about our organisation, please browse our website (www.astronauticalcentre.com) or contact us at info@astronauticalcentre.com

Name: SUAS Aerospace
Description: Irish for UP! SUAS Aerospace is a private upstream space service provider based in the Republic of Ireland. SUAS will facilitate the critical test and launch capabilities of the European space sector with a dedicated rocket engine test site and orbital spaceport on the west coast of Ireland. SUAS’ spaceport will provide access to polar orbits from a location with a temperate climate, within the European Union, and with excellent logistical connections to mainland Europe.

Name: EirSpace
Description:
EirSpace is a nonprofit organisation based in Dublin, Ireland, with the aim of providing students with practical experience in the aerospace industry and promoting the expansion of the aerospace sector in Ireland. We have a growing team, with current projects spanning rocketry and unmanned aerial systems.

As EirSpace is not affiliated with any one university, we have the advantage of being able to draw talent from institutions across Dublin.
Our current achievements include holding the records for the fastest and highest rocket ever launched by a student team from Irish soil, as well as completing the construction and flight testing of our first UAV.
We aim to enter our first international rocketry competition in June 2026 and our first UAV competition in 2027.

Join us as we push the boundaries of aerospace in Ireland.

Contact: management@eirspace.org

Name: ESA Space Solutions Centre Ireland
Description:
ESA Space Solutions Centre Ireland was established in 2016 and is headquartered in Tyndall National Institute, a leading European research centre in integrated ICT (Information and Communications Technology) hardware and systems.
ESA Space Solutions Centre Ireland is part of the largest space innovation network in the world. Across ESA Member States the ESA Space Solutions network is supporting European start-ups and SMEs to develop businesses using space technology and data. It does this by providing funding, business and technical support to help generate successful businesses and create sustainable jobs. As a constituent member of this network ESA Space Solutions Centre Ireland is the go-to place for great businesses that use space to improve everyday life. 
Space is an industry sector of growing importance in Ireland as reflected by the publication of the National Space Strategy for Enterprise 2019-2025 in June 2019. The space sector offers a plethora of commercial opportunities to Irish companies, with significant supports now being targeted at those developing downstream or terrestrial applications.
At ESA Space Solutions Centre Ireland we are supporting Irish companies (start ups and established companies) through a range of different initiatives, namely:
ESA Business Incubation Centre (BIC) Ireland
ESA Spark Funding Programme
ESA Space Solutions Ireland is composed of five Consortium Partners. These are the Tyndall National Institute (Lead Partner), Athlone Institute of Technology, Maynooth University, MaREI and University College Dublin.
Our local partner is Enterprise Ireland, which acts as the contact point for Ireland’s National Delegation to ESA along with the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment.

Name: NASA International Space Apps Challenge Dublin
Description:
A Community In & Out Of This World!

Returning to Dublin on October 4 and 5, 2025, NASA International Space Apps Challenge is the largest annual global hackathon on the planet. Growing since 2012, the 2022 edition built a collaboration of 93,520 registered participants, 15,444 teams across 485 local events in 163 countries and territories.

The event offers space and time for coders, scientists, artists, designers, storytellers, makers, builders, entrepreneurs, technologists, and other innovators around the world to come together and use NASA and partner space agencies' open data to create solutions to real challenges we face on Earth and in space.

There’s Always Space For One More!

NASA International Space Apps Challenge is open to everyone, including those who have never “hacked" before. 
In fact, teams with the most diverse sets of skills are often the most successful
All ages, skill levels, social, cultural and professional backgrounds are welcome to join the community.

Stay tuned for mission updates!

Name: SATERA
Description:
SPACE-BASED COMPOSITE ADS-B AND MULTILATERATION SYSTEM VALIDATION THROUGH SCALABLE SIMULATIONS (SATERA) will propose and validate an integrity estimator for space-based ADS-B systems based on crosschecking positions reported in ADS-B messages with position estimations provided by space-based MLAT systems.

To reach this goal, SATERA will apply a stepped approach starting by the definition of  high-level operational descriptions, identifying all the involved stakeholders, and detailing the CNS equipage of the fleet and the available air traffic services. 
The research team will develop theoretical models to assess and benchmark the proposed system architecture leading to a full list of functional requirements and interfaces description.

SATERA will develop a system performance prediction tool to compute the theoretical performance of a MLAT system whose receiving stations are onboard of a  constellation of LEO small satellites. This tool will take into consideration all the error sources that can affect the MLAT system performance and will be used to select the most suitable constellation.
For validating the SATERA solution also end-to-end system evaluation  tool that will be developed. Several validation exercises addressing the provision of composite space- based ADS-B+MLAT surveillance in the EURSAM and NAT corridors for realistic traffic will be done.

Name: UCD Centre for Space Research (C-Space)
Description:
The Centre for Space Research (C-Space) is based at University College Dublin (UCD) in Ireland. It is the university-wide hub dedicated to advancing space-related research, innovation, and education. Established in 2020 as Ireland’s first dedicated centre of its kind, C-Space serves as a strategic leader for the sector, uniting "upstream" activities like satellite systems and payload instrumentation, with "downstream" applications such as Earth Observation and data analytics.

Our work is inherently interdisciplinary, bringing together researchers across the Sciences, Engineering, Social Sciences, Humanities and Health to address the great scientific and societal questions of our time. From the historic success of EIRSAT-1, Ireland’s first satellite, to cutting-edge research in astrophysics and space policy, C-Space acts as a vital bridge between academia, industry, and international agencies like the European Space Agency (ESA).

By fostering world-class collaboration and supporting a robust educational pipeline, we aim to position Ireland as a global leader in the space economy while ensuring the sustainable and responsible use of space for future generations.

Name: SQAT project
Description:
SQAT is a 3.5-year project, funded under the Horizon Europe Programme, that focuses on Implementing Smart Farming Applications using EO Data, Soil Sensors & Robotics.

SQAT's smart soil mapping service is a multi-level, multi-technology and multi-purpose solution. With a keen eye on markets and users, SQAT’s approach is designed to overcome today’s practical, technical and financial challenges to generate high resolution soil properties maps and demand-driven products like application maps for soil improvement or crop management, or compliancy proof for eco schemes. Our vision is that the integration of different technologies provides a flexible and agile service beating the unbundled alternatives that are now in the market: our in-situ sampling and/or sensoring is wrapped in a Copernicus-based artificial intelligence soil mapping product.

Name: VOTE TRA
Description:
Digital Voting Hub for Sustainable Urban Transport System

The Challenge
Citizens are the focal point of improving urban transport systems. They are important because they can depict the actual demands and expectations of the passengers. When we involve the citizens in the decision-making process, we guarantee adopting more efficient outcomes.

The Solution
We propose creating a digital voting hub to make the participation process for evaluating and developing the transport system in urban areas more efficient, flexible and demand-based. Allowing citizens, the option to vote through the digital voting hub increases voter turnout and considers the actual expectation of passengers.

Name: National Space Subsystems & Payloads Initiative
Description:
The National Space Subsystems and Payloads Initiative (NSSPI), funded by the Irish Government's Disruptive Technologies Innovation Fund, aims to advance space technology development through collaboration, expertise, and research, positioning Ireland as a recognised hub of space excellence. Total value of DTIF Award is €7.9 million.

The project is organised into clusters:
1) Optical Communications for Space 
2) Autonomous Smart Satellites
3) Spacecraft and Payload Modelling, Simulation, Assembly, Integration and Test research support

The project is being carried out through a partnership between the UCD Colleges of Engineering & Architecture and Science, and six industry partners. The industry partners are Réaltra, Ubotica, Altera/Intel, Mbryonics, Equal1 and ÉireComposites.
